senses.sense_definition: To surprise someone unexpectedly in a way that often causes harm or confusion; to catch completely off guard.

examples.text: The company's sudden decision to close the branch completely <w>blindsided</w> the workers.
She felt <w>blindsided</w> when her business partner resigned without any prior warning.

senses.sense_definition: To physically hit or attack someone from a direction where they cannot see it coming.

examples.text: The defender managed to <w>blindside</w> the quarterback before he could throw the ball.
A mugger emerged from the alley and <w>blindsided</w> the unsuspecting pedestrian.

senses.sense_definition: An area or side where a person, especially a driver, has obstructed vision.

examples.text: Always check your mirrors because a motorcycle might be hidden in your <w>blindside</w>.
The lorry hit the barrier on its <w>blindside</w> while turning sharply.

senses.sense_definition: A person's particular weakness or vulnerability that they may not be aware of.

examples.text: His arrogance was his obvious <w>blindside</w> during the negotiations.
Opponents in the debate focused heavily on the candidate's <w>blindside</w>.

senses.sense_definition: In rugby, the narrower side of the field between a scrum or breakdown and the nearest touchline.

examples.text: The scrum-half decided to attack down the <w>blindside</w> to catch the defense out.
There was very little space available on the <w>blindside</w> for the winger to run.

senses.sense_definition: A blindside flanker in rugby union, typically wearing the number six jersey.

examples.text: The team needs a physical player to start as the <w>blindside</w> this weekend.
He played brilliantly at <w>blindside</w> throughout the entire international tournament.
